title: Split the cli spec: move the retention and transition-history requirements REQ-cli-018 and REQ-cli-025 to REQ-cli-027 to a new history module as REQ-history-001 to REQ-history-004 with wording unchanged and a documented ID mapping, so the cli requirements companion has headroom under the 65536-byte record bound
description: Split the cli spec: move the retention and transition-history requirements REQ-cli-018 and REQ-cli-025 to REQ-cli-027 to a new history module as REQ-history-001 to REQ-history-004 with wording unchanged and a documented ID mapping, so the cli requirements companion has headroom under the 65536-byte record bound
acceptance_criteria: specs/history is a new module that owns src/history.rs, tests/history.rs and tests/evidence.rs and holds REQ-history-001 to REQ-history-004, each with the exact wording of REQ-cli-018, REQ-cli-025, REQ-cli-026 and REQ-cli-027; the old IDs are removed from specs/cli and become tombstones

A test proves the move lost nothing: every moved requirement body has the SHA-256 it had at main 7bd1b62, every REQ-cli ID from 001 to 032 is either still in specs/cli or mapped, and a one-time before/after comparison of all 32 blocks is recorded

The ID mapping is documented in docs/FRD.md and the history module context, and the cases that link the moved requirements move to .chough/cases/history.cases.toml under a documented case ID mapping with their bindings unchanged
specs/cli/requirements.md is at most 59000 bytes, the record limit stays 65536 and no requirement, case binding or test is weakened
fmt, lint, the full tests, every moved case and fledge lanes run verify pass

answers.constraints: AGENTS.md: preserve existing files and records; never invent results. SpecSync requires REQ-<module>-<number> IDs per delta module and keeps removed IDs as permanent tombstones, so moved requirements get new history IDs with a documented mapping. Archived changes, evidence and bug records stay untouched. Parent agent instruction 2026-11-03 9:46 AM MT: split rather than raise the limit, keep wording, do not weaken anything
